## v2.8.0 Release notes

This release brings together the features, fixes, and maintenance changes since v2.7.0. It adds IPv6 dual-stack and IPv6-only network support, custom DNS (including DoH and DoT), a global default routing rule, and one-click network diagnostics. It fixes adapters being wrongly shown as "Cooldown" during aggregation, which could make aggregation slower than a single adapter. The installer now performs recoverable installs and a native update handoff, and automatic recovery after network changes is improved.

### Aggregation speed and adapter health

- Fixed an adapter showing "Cooldown" during aggregation even though it was working. Previously a failed IPv6 connection cooled down the whole adapter, so new connections (for example Steam downloads) were concentrated on the slower adapter and aggregation became slower. IPv4 and IPv6 health are now tracked separately, so unavailable IPv6 no longer affects the adapter's IPv4 traffic.
- When a router hands out only unique local IPv6 addresses (ULA, `fc00::/7`) without an IPv6 default gateway, the adapter is no longer treated as having IPv6 egress, which previously made connections fail after IPv6 was taken over. NAT66 setups with an IPv6 gateway and public IPv6 are unaffected.
- Stable IPv6 addresses are preferred while privacy (temporary) addresses rotate, reducing unnecessary connection rebuilds.
- The per-datagram UDP forwarding path has far less lock contention and allocation, lowering CPU use at high packet rates such as games and QUIC.

### IPv6 and DNS

- Supports IPv6 adapter discovery, per-family DNS binding, staggered dual-stack connections (IPv6 first, IPv4 fallback), NAT64/DNS64, and TCP/UDP forwarding on IPv6-only networks. The home page shows IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and availability separately.
- Added custom DNS: configure multiple plain DNS, DoH, and DoT servers; TUN mode uses the matching resolver pool. Canceling DoT now waits for connection cleanup.
- Before TUN starts, the system-direct egress is pinned and the DNS egress is verified; on failure HypoMux falls back before the virtual adapter is enabled, reducing cases where the network is unusable after startup.

### Routing rules

- Added a global default rule (Settings → Advanced network): traffic that matches no manual rule or rule set can use multi-adapter aggregation (default), direct, reject, or a specific adapter. Applies the next time TUN starts.
- When the global default is reject, HypoMux no longer keeps warning that the external connectivity probe failed just because the probe is rejected by that rule.
- Rules are selected only through their checkboxes to avoid accidental row selection; on Windows, rule-set file replacement is retried when the file is in use.

### Network changes and diagnostics

- Aggregation bindings are rebuilt automatically after an adapter's address, index, or DNS changes. Monitoring runs in the background independently of the UI. While an adapter is temporarily disconnected the remaining adapters keep working, and it rejoins when it recovers.
- Added one-click Windows network diagnostics that collect adapter, route, DNS, proxy, and HypoMux status for bug reports. Diagnostics verify TLS and report inconclusive results as such.
- Tunnel-type virtual adapters are classified correctly, and IPv6 probe failures report their cause.

### Aggregation hotspot (experimental)

- With the adaptive speed strategy, new UDP flows (including game and QUIC traffic from hotspot devices) are also allocated by each adapter's measured throughput; established UDP flows keep their adapter.
- You can now choose which wireless adapter broadcasts the hotspot.

### Installation and updates

- The installer now performs a recoverable, transactional install: new files are staged and verified before they are written, and a failed or canceled install restores the previous version and service configuration. A failed WebView2 installation is reported explicitly.
- In-app updates launch the installer through a native handoff and support non-ASCII paths. Stalled downloads are stopped automatically, retries reuse an already verified installer, and the installer is kept when installation fails or is canceled.
- Added a script that collects installation diagnostics.

### Security and stability

- The HTTP proxy forwards each plain HTTP request as its own framed message, so later requests on the same connection cannot be sent to the wrong site. Header read time and size are bounded.
- System proxy restoration is journaled before registry writes so an interrupted restore can resume, and external edits are preserved.
- Updated the Go toolchain and vulnerable network dependencies; added a global switch for AI features.
- Port settings are validated and telemetry failures are reported. Fixed shortcuts firing during IME input, overflowing diagnostic reports, and settings layout and scrolling issues.

### Upgrade and usage notes

- This is the **v2.8.0 stable release** for Windows 10/11 x64. Use the official installer to update both the desktop app and Core, then restart aggregation/TUN.
- Updating in-app from v2.7.0 still uses the v2.7.0 updater to launch the installer. If the automatic update fails, download the installer from the website or the release page and install it manually.
- Aggregation and Steam optimization do not guarantee higher speed and never split a single TCP connection across links. When adapter speeds differ greatly, the slower adapter may still receive some new connections.
- In HTTP proxy mode (not TUN), each plain HTTP request uses its own upstream connection.
